findings.claim: arkcli panel had backend errors; review is partial
findings.why: [panel:arkcli] At least one arkcli reviewer failed, so PASS only means the completed panel members found no blocker.

findings.claim: Integration selftest covers only one closure-blocking path
findings.why: [panel:claude] The subprocess pipeline test proves `output_gate → run_gate` works for the "closed fronts + missing independent review" case. But it doesn't test end-to-end blocking for: (a) open fronts present, (b) missing CodexCompletionReview, (c) missing retrospective proof. Unit-level tests in run_gate's own selftest cover these individually, but no integration test proves the full hook pipeline for each blocking reason.

findings.claim: Empty-frontier fallback weakens Coda gate specificity
findings.why: [panel:claude] When `_fallback_protocol_state` finds no F-id sections (frontier.md emptied, all fronts closed, or no H2-H6 F-id headings), `active_fronts` is empty. The Coda gate then requires only a `process_anchor` match (e.g. `复审` alone is sufficient). This is weaker than the active-front path which requires a specific F-id. A run that accidentally has an empty/junk frontier.md could cycle through generic Codas without re-reading the canonical state. Disposition explicitly accepts this as the documented tradeoff, but an external reviewer should flag it.

findings.claim: selftest_all.log is summary-only — no per-assertion trace
findings.why: [panel:claude] The 54-line log gives PASS/FAIL per suite, not per assertion. The output_gate selftest alone has ~40 individual checks; a reviewer cannot confirm which specific assertions were exercised. The selftest framework guarantees that any single failure fails the suite, so "PASS" implies all checks passed — but the evidence is a derived artifact (environment-provided log) rather than raw assertion output.

findings.claim: Free-form retrospective section bypasses per-item validation
findings.why: [panel:claude] `_retro_framework_items` splits on `Problem:` fields or numbered/heading patterns. When a retrospective uses neither (one prose paragraph listing multiple issues), the entire Framework problems section is treated as one item. One `Status: open` line with one `Residual risk:` satisfies the gate for all issues in the paragraph. Disposition acknowledges this as legacy compatibility support — not a regression, but a residual enforcement gap.

[panel:claude] `_cookie_expired` returns `False` on `TypeError`/`ValueError`/`OverflowError` from `parsedate_to_datetime`. For a security toolkit doing red-team work, keeping a cookie with an unparseable Expires is the functional-correct choice (don't break sessions), but it's worth noting that a server sending maliciously malformed Expires headers could force stale cookies to persist. Design tradeoff, not a bug — acknowledged in prior reviews.

blind_spots: [claude] **Symlink escape from runs_root is correctly mitigated but not regression-tested**: `_run_from_pointer` resolves symlinks via `candidate.resolve()` then checks `run_dir.relative_to(root)` (anti_drift.diff:51-55). If a pointer points to a symlink outside runs_root, the resolved path fails `relative_to()` and is rejected. This is correct, but no selftest exercises a symlink specifically.
[claude] **`~` expansion is coded (anti_drift.diff:49: `Path(raw).expanduser()`) but never regression-tested with a path containing `~`**: selftests only use absolute paths in temp directories.

[claude] **`_merge_cookies_into_headers` default (explicit Cookie > jar) is correct**: The selftest at probe.diff:253-257 proves `same=explicit` wins over `same=jar`. ✓ The preflight path (probe.diff:162-163) builds from `dict(jar)` then overlays `original_explicit_cookies`, then overlays fresh `cookie_updates` — matching browser precedence (fresh Set-Cookie > explicit request Cookie > stored jar).

[claude] **Cookie jar atomic write (probe.diff:79-86)**: Uses `NamedTemporaryFile(write)` + `os.chmod(0o600)` + `Path.replace()`. On macOS (the deployment target), tempfile defaults to 0o600. On Linux with permissive umask, there's a brief TOCTOU window before chmod. Accepted platform limitation.

[claude] **`_retro_framework_items` splitting covers three formats**: `Problem:` prefix, numbered (`1.`, `2)`, `3、`), and H3-H6 headings. A retrospective using bullet items without `Problem:` prefix (e.g. `- First tool issue\n- Status: fixed`) would NOT be split — the whole section would be one item. The template instructs users to use numbered/Problem/heading formats, so this is a documentation-convention gap more than a code gap.

[claude] **The 8-round review hardening process was thorough**: Vague Coda bypasses → fixed (R3). Multi-action conjunction gaps (`和`, bare `and`) → fixed (R4). Verb-list gaps, timezone-naive expiry, heading spoof → fixed (R5). Monolithic diff truncation → fixed (R6). run_gate review fallback → fixed (R7, fail-closed). Coda for zero-active-front run → fixed (R8). Each round found real gaps and they were resolved.

[claude] **No safety regression**: Every change either tightens enforcement (stricter Coda, stricter review/retrospective gates, fail-closed boundaries) or fixes correctness bugs (cookie precedence/deletion/atomicity, coverage mention-only verdicts, active-run identity). Nothing weakens an existing boundary.

[claude] **Chinese regex quality**: The Coda enforcement's Chinese pattern matching (`_ACTION_WORDS_ZH`, vague phrase deny-list, multi-action conjunctions) is layered (vague check → concrete anchor → action-verb check → multi-action check). The deny-list approach for vague phrases is inherently incomplete for a morphologically rich language, but the defense-in-depth with the concrete-anchor and action-verb checks provides strong coverage.
